title: Identification of the finite root linearization
statement: For a prime l, a finite extension E of the l-adic rationals, a scheme T, Chern data c [def-sp-tower-class-chern] and a finite level n, evaluate the inverse rootForget, apply the evaluated forgotten ordinary scalar unit on c.rootModule, then finiteScalarForgetIso [def-sfb-finite-forget-comparison] and the forgotten lineEvaluation. This composite from the roots sheaf to the finite coefficient line equals finiteRootMap [def-sp-tower-class-finite].

source.place: clause (2), scalar extension and finite evaluation

proof.text: Given a root section z, transport it by rootForget inverse and the section equality of Forget to an actual section x of c.rootModule. The ordinary unit_section equation identifies its scalar unit image with scalarExtensionSection.

The comparison finiteScalarForgetIso retains that section. Apply the pure-tensor equation of lineEvaluation with scalar one and cancel rootForget with its inverse. The candidate sends z to one tensor z, hence uniqueness of finiteRootMap identifies it.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteBoundary_rootMap (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    {T : Scheme.{u}} (c : Chern l E T) (n : ℕ) :
    (abEvaluation T n).map c.rootForget.inv ≫
      (c.reduction.forget.F ⋙ abEvaluation T n).map
        (c.scalar.ordinaryAdjunction.unit.app c.rootModule) ≫
      (finiteScalarForgetIso l E c n).hom.app (lineModule l E c) ≫
      (finiteForget l E T n).map (lineEvaluation l E c n).hom =
      finiteRootMap l E T n
